title: B2-22 · Expose and argue by voice

blocks.text: B2-22 · Expose and argue by voice

In B2-10 you have learned to write an argumentative text; in B2-17 to speak a fuṣḥā natural speech; in EGY-18 to present in Egyptian educated. Now put the three things together for a central exam task B2: expose a topic for four to five minutes in front of an audience and argue in voice in a discussion, answering questions and objections. The rules change by voice: listeners cannot go back, so they need an announced structure, clear signals of passage, shorter sentences, useful repetitions, concrete examples. In this unit learn the structure of an intervention, the signals of the oral speech, the techniques to convince without manipulating, the way to handle questions and objections and to take and give up the word in a debate. Three weeks, in parallel with the end of MAG-02 and the beginning of MAG-03.

rows: B2 · Module B2.4 Variation and production
16–18 hours · three weeks (weeks 239–241), plus the MAG track in separate blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a recorder (also the phone), a stopwatch, sessions with the tutor; if possible, a small audience (course partners)
Targets. At the end of the lesson you know:
1. prepare a playlist for four to five minutes without writing the complete text;
2. to open, develop and close an intervention with the signals of the oral speech;
3. use examples, data and rhetorical questions to convince, avoiding fallacies (B2-10);
4. handle questions, objections and interruptions with grace and precision;
5. to take, hold and give up the floor in a debate in fuṣḥā Talked.

blocks.text: The fallacies of B2-10 (generalization, false dilemma, attack on the person) are more frequent and more dangerous, because the listener has less time to notice. Avoid it even when the audience applauds.

Voice, pauses and rhythm. 1) Speed: in an intervention we speak more slowly than in conversation; about 110–130 words per minute. 2) Pause: a short break after each passing signal ( ⁧أَنْتَقِلُ الآنَ إِلَى⁩ ... pause), a longer break before the final sentence. 3) Emphasis: slightly raises the voice on the keyword and slows down on numbers. 4) Fuṣḥā spoken (B2-17): desinences only where they are natural, internal vowels always correct. Register, timer, listen again: it's the fastest way to improve.
